answer:
To find the area of the parallelogram with vertices \(\bold{0}\), \(\bold{v}\), \(\bold{w}\), and \(\bold{v} + \bold{w}\) where \(\bold{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\bold{w} = \begin{pmatrix} 11 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\), we use the determinant of the matrix formed by these vectors.

The matrix formed by \(\bold{v}\) and \(\bold{w}\) as columns is:
\[
\begin{pmatrix} 5 & 11 \\ -3 & -2 \end{pmatrix}
\]

The determinant of this matrix is calculated as follows:
\[
\text{det} = (5)(-2) - (-3)(11) = -10 + 33 = 23
\]

The absolute value of this determinant gives the area of the parallelogram:
\[
\text{Area} = |23| = 23
\]

Thus, the area of the parallelogram is \(\boxed{23}\).
